thread:
Lexi (support): FYI customer 54621 is seeing SSE responses get cut off mid-stream when they sit behind a GCP HTTPS LB + Cloud Run stack. They say partial tokens stop arriving but connection stays open, then client reconnects and gets duplicates. Case: CS-54621.

Dan K: any known h2->h1 translation weirdness? :thinking_face:

Maya Chen: yeah we've seen intermediaries buffer until connection close, which collapses streaming semantics. But "connection stays open" makes me think something else (maybe payload limiter or 502->empty body). Do we have client pcap / server logs?

Lexi (support): customer attached short logs and a minimal repro. They use EventSource polyfill in a mobile webview and our hosted endpoint via `https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream`. They included this curl attempt:

```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-alpha"
```

But their network team reports an internal gateway that upgrades to HTTP/2 on the client side then proxies to Cloud Run over HTTP/1.1.

Kevin R: important detail: Cloud Run's HTTP/1.1 frontends can and do add `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and might buffer small chunks depending on proxy settings. Also some gRPC gateways (envoy/nginx) can coalesce frames. If the client expects SSE chunk boundaries, collapsing can look like partial outputs or sudden end-of-stream.

Dan K: they also mentioned short-lived JWT refresh mid-stream. If the auth layer returns `401` for a sub-request or token rotate path that isn't handled by the stream proxy, that could cause backend to send an error frame or terminate streams. Any 401/403 in our logs around the session?

Lexi (support): attached a small excerpt from their client log: "EventSource received 'open' then 2 data events then nothing, connection stays OPEN, after ~35s polyfill reconnects and receives duplicate first 2 events then new partial output."

Maya Chen: That pattern smells like the intermediary swallowed the FIN/chunk-terminator and left the TCP connection alive, so client-side SSE polyfill keeps waiting. When reconnection happens, server replays last tokens (we do incremental token idempotency) and they see duplicates. Could also be a proxy GOAWAY/stream reset that the polyfill didn't surface.

engops-bot: alert: backend-host-17 reported `GRPC: RST_STREAM (refused_stream)` at 2026-01-15T10:12:03Z for connection id a3f5.

Kevin R: if we have a RST_STREAM/GOAWAY on the server connection, the front proxy (H2) might translate that into a silent connection drop on the H1 side or attempt retry semantics. That can manifest as partial message delivery.

Dan K: repro plan: 1) replicate with a local H2->H1 proxy that converts to chunked; 2) reproduce token rotation during stream and observe. I've got a tiny repro script using `node` and `nghttp2` that toggles a reject mid-stream.

Maya Chen: add another axis: test with direct curl (no LB) to determine whether it's our runtime or the intermediate. If direct to a dedicated server (or via `--http2`) works fine but LB path fails, it's proxy.

Lexi (support): customer asked for quick mitigations — what can we tell them while we debug?

Kevin R: advise: 1) If possible, disable H2->H1 translation on the fronting gateway (use passthrough) or configure the LB not to buffer for SSE endpoints. On GCP, ensure `enableStreamTimeout` is off and check backend service `connection_termination` settings. 2) Make sure proxies forward `Transfer-Encoding` and don't inject `Content-Length`. 3) If tokens rotate during long streams, use a refresh mechanism that doesn't drop the connection or consider pre-warming a long-lived token.

Dan K: for our side, we can add a short-lived keepalive comment every 10s (SSE comment `: keepalive\n\n`) from the runtime to force proxies to flush. Do we already have that?

Maya Chen: we do emit keepalive pings on certain routes but not all. We should consider enabling them for chat/stream endpoints by default to handle intermediate buffering. However we must ensure this doesn't change billing semantics.

Lexi (support): customer tried `--no-buffer` on their fetch polyfill and saw slight improvement. They're okay testing config changes. They also sent a pcap showing TCP keeps alive but no SSE frames for ~30s.

Dan K: action items: 
- Kevin: check Cloud Run / LB logs for connection-level GOAWAY / reset between `10:10:50` and `10:13:00` (customer time) and share back.
- Maya: prototype enabling a keepalive comment on streaming route (feature flag) and run quick A/B.
- Dan: reproduce locally with nghttpx/Envoy H2->H1 translation with token rotate mid-stream. Add repro script to internal gist.
- Lexi: tell customer steps to disable buffering on their proxy and to avoid token rotate mid-stream while we investigate.

Kevin R: noted. If we confirm the LB is coalescing, mitigation is to either 1) switch to a direct H2 pass-through (preferred) or 2) stricter keepalives and idempotent reconnection logic on client. Also flagging for infra: add metrics for stream truncation / duplicate event reconnections so we can detect at scale.

Maya Chen: quick note on duplicates — we can include an `event_id` header per SSE data packet which clients can dedupe on reconnect. API change but small (header `X-Redwood-Event-Id` or SSE `id:` field). Could help customers until proxies are fixed.

Lexi (support): I'll tell the customer the temporary checklist + ask them to run the direct curl test and share raw tcpdump. Also ask for their gateway config snippet (nginx/envoy).

engops-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag "sse-keepalive" to staging at 2026-01-15T11:30:00Z.

Dan K: excellent. Keep me in the loop; I'll post repro gist in #eng-runtime when ready.

Maya Chen: if we don't hear back in 48h, we'll escalate to incident review and consider adding default keepalive.

Lexi (support): thanks team — updating CS-54621 with the recommended steps and linking this thread. :thumbsup:
